introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Further Mathematics 3 (0775), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2022. Duration: two and a half hours.**

Answer ALL questions. For your guidance the approximate mark allocation for parts of each question is indicated in brackets. Mathematical formulae and tables, published by the Board, and noiseless non-programmable electronic calculators are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage.
enonce_intro_markdown: A particle $P$ of mass $m$ falls from rest in a medium which offers a resistance to motion of magnitude $\dfrac{mgv^2}{U^2}\ \mathrm{N}$ where $v\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ is the speed and $U$ is a positive constant.

questions.enonce_markdown: Show that when the speed of $P$ is $\dfrac{3}{5}U$, $P$ has fallen a distance $\dfrac{U^2}{g}\ln\left(\dfrac{5}{4}\right)$. *[7 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Let $x$ be the distance fallen, measured downwards, so the acceleration is $v\dfrac{dv}{dx}$. Newton's second law (weight $mg$ down, resistance up):

$$mv\frac{dv}{dx} = mg - \frac{mgv^2}{U^2} \;\Longrightarrow\; v\frac{dv}{dx} = g\left(1-\frac{v^2}{U^2}\right).$$

Separate the variables; $P$ starts from rest ($v=0$ at $x=0$):

$$\int_0^{3U/5}\frac{v}{1-\dfrac{v^2}{U^2}}\,dv = \int_0^{x} g\,dx.$$

The left-hand side is

$$\left[-\frac{U^2}{2}\ln\left(1-\frac{v^2}{U^2}\right)\right]_0^{3U/5} = -\frac{U^2}{2}\ln\left(1-\frac{9}{25}\right) = -\frac{U^2}{2}\ln\frac{16}{25} = \frac{U^2}{2}\ln\frac{25}{16} = U^2\ln\frac54.$$

Hence $gx = U^2\ln\dfrac54$, that is

$$x = \frac{U^2}{g}\ln\left(\frac54\right).$$

questions.enonce_markdown: Find the time taken by $P$ to attain the speed of $\dfrac{3}{5}U$. *[6 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
With time as the variable, $m\dfrac{dv}{dt} = mg - \dfrac{mgv^2}{U^2}$, so

$$\frac{dv}{dt} = \frac{g\,(U^2-v^2)}{U^2} \;\Longrightarrow\; \int_0^{3U/5}\frac{U^2}{U^2-v^2}\,dv = \int_0^t g\,dt = gt.$$

By partial fractions, $\dfrac{U^2}{U^2-v^2} = \dfrac U2\left(\dfrac{1}{U-v}+\dfrac{1}{U+v}\right)$, so

$$gt = \frac U2\Big[\ln(U+v) - \ln(U-v)\Big]_0^{3U/5} = \frac U2\ln\left(\frac{8U/5}{2U/5}\right) = \frac U2\ln 4 = U\ln 2.$$

$$t = \frac{U}{g}\ln 2.$$
